items.reason: magpie: a mature (10.7k stars, MIT) local gateway letting coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) route across other providers' API keys/subscriptions, with failover groups. Real running infra-adjacent tool, but it's a convenience/arbitrage proxy rather than new serving technique, and it reads other agents' keychain-stored credentials by design -- a minor trust wrinkle worth flagging, not surfacing as a headline.
key_facts: ~10.7k stars, 716 forks, 3,171 commits, MIT license, no outside PRs accepted
Local gateway at 127.0.0.1:3425 that lets Claude Code/Codex/Gemini CLI use other providers' models via existing subscriptions or API keys
Reads sign-in data from other agents' files and the macOS Keychain to find usable subscriptions
Sends a daily anonymous usage ping by default (opt-out via settings or DO_NOT_TRACK=1)

items.title: Zod 4.6.6 compromised by malware?
items.reason: Verified directly: zod/@zod/mini 4.6.6's commit diff adds a minified meta.test.mjs wired into preinstall that resolves an Ethereum-contract-stored domain (EtherHiding-style C2), fetches a base64 setup+payload bundle, and executes it via a data: URL import at install time -- classic npm supply-chain backdoor pattern, no maintainer explanation in the commit. zod is one of the most widely depended-on JS/TS validation libraries, including as the schema layer in a lot of LLM tool-calling/agent-framework code, so the blast radius if confirmed malicious is large even though this is pure-cyber rather than AI research itself.
key_facts: Commit d821685 bumps zod/@zod/mini 4.6.5->4.6.6, titled 'Fix bugs and improve performance'
Adds meta.test.mjs (minified) wired via package.json `preinstall` hook in both packages
meta.test.mjs queries an Ethereum contract via public RPC, decodes the result as a domain, fetches https://<domain>/loader
Response contains base64 setup script + base64 payload; setup is run via a data: URL import, payload written to temp dir then deleted
release.yml changed to trigger on any push to main touching version files, removing a comment that said a version bump alone doesn't publish and a maintainer must approve the npm release
